import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Period of $p$-th powers modulo $n$

a: Period of cubes mod $n$.
The $n$-th term $a(n)$ is the smallest positive integer $T$ such that
$\forall k \in \mathbb{N}$, $(k+T)^3 \equiv k^3 \pmod n$.

The length of the minimal positive period of the sequence $k^p \pmod n$.
$a_p(n) = \min \{ T \in \mathbb{N}^+ \mid \forall k \in \mathbb{N}, (k+T)^p \equiv k^p \pmod n \}$.

*References:*
- [A282779](https://oeis.org/A282779)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
-/

namespace OeisA282779


open Nat Set

/--
Period of cubes mod $n$.
The $n$-th term $a(n)$ is the smallest positive integer $T$ such that
$\forall k \in \mathbb{N}$, $(k+T)^3 \equiv k^3 \pmod n$.
-/
noncomputable def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  if n = 0 then 0 -- Handle the non-sequence index n=0
  else
    -- sInf computes the infimum of the set, which is the minimum since ℕ is well-ordered.
    sInf { T : ℕ | 0 < T ∧ ∀ k : ℕ, (k + T) ^ 3 % n = k ^ 3 % n }

/--
The length of the minimal positive period of the sequence $k^p \pmod n$.
$a_p(n) = \min \{ T \in \mathbb{N}^+ \mid \forall k \in \mathbb{N}, (k+T)^p \equiv k^p \pmod n \}$.
-/
noncomputable def periodOfPowerMod (p n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  if n = 0 then 0
  else
    sInf { T : ℕ | 0 < T ∧ ∀ k : ℕ, (k + T) ^ p % n = k ^ p % n }



/--
Conjecture: let $a_p(n)$ be the length of the period of the sequence $k^p \bmod n$ where $p$ is a prime, then $a_p(n) = n/p$ if $n \equiv 0 \pmod{p^2}$, else $a_p(n) = n$.

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/282779.wip.lean#L104"]
theorem periodOfPowerMod_eq (p n : ℕ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hn : n > 0) :
    periodOfPowerMod p n = if p ^ 2 ∣ n then n / p else n := by
    sorry


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by exact periodOfPowerMod_eq 3 1 (by decide) (by decide)

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_2 : a 2 = 2 := by exact periodOfPowerMod_eq 3 2 (by decide) (by decide)

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = 3 := by exact periodOfPowerMod_eq 3 3 (by decide) (by decide)

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 4 := by exact periodOfPowerMod_eq 3 4 (by decide) (by decide)

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_5 : a 5 = 5 := by exact periodOfPowerMod_eq 3 5 (by decide) (by decide)

end OeisA282779

reformulations.difference: OEIS illustrates the power sequence starting at k=1; Lean requires the period identity for every natural k, including zero, and defines the least positive period using sInf. The same conventions occur in OeisA282779.a.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n>0, powers modulo n depend only on the input modulo n. Any period identity holding at all positive indices therefore holds at an arbitrary natural index k by applying it at k+n. Moreover, T=n is always a positive period, so the set used by sInf is nonempty and its natural-number infimum is its least element. The complete equivalence with the positive-index least-period specification was proved as Review282779.period_eq_iff_source in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without sorry or the reviewed theorem. Also, a n = periodOfPowerMod 3 n is definitional.

review.notes: All eight declarations were checked. The n=0 guards merely extend definitions outside OEIS's domain (offset 1); the main theorem explicitly assumes n>0. Primality excludes division by zero, and p² ∣ n makes n/p exact. Independently proved all five test lemmas and additional boundary cases, including p=2 and the source's p=7,n=98 example. Finite searches found no formula discrepancies for p in {2,3,5,7,11,13} and 1≤n≤250; all 10,000 b-file entries agree with the cube formula. OEIS explicitly records the conjecture as proved. Its linked AlphaProof Nexus artifact, adapted only for the current import and one renamed Mathlib lemma, compiled and proved the exact reviewed statement with axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. The main OEIS HTML page was blocked, so its official data mirror was used. No repository files were edited.
